notes: The battery pack and motors have their own attached red/black leads, so no separate jumper wires are used; the lead ends are clamped directly in the board's screw terminal blocks.
Battery red wire goes to VIN and black to GND, as the manual requires.
The manual says the motors can be connected either way round, so which motor lead goes to A or B is arbitrary. Motor 1 is assumed to be on M1 and motor 2 on M2.
The photos show a generic Pi (probably a 3B-style board), but the catalogue match is rpi-4b, which was used as given.
The board sits on the Pi's GPIO header and uses GPIO 7, 8, 9 and 10 for motor control. This is modelled as the single gpio-header to GPIO_HEADER join.
The battery pack's ON/OFF switch must be off while wiring. It is not modelled.
